definitions.explanation: A type of battery that uses a paste electrolyte rather than liquid, commonly used in everyday devices like remote controls, flashlights, and toys.

examples.japanese: {乾電池|かんでんち}を{入|い}れ{替|か}える。
{乾電池|かんでんち}が{切|き}れた。
この{懐中電灯|かいちゅうでんとう}は{単三|たんさん}{乾電池|かんでんち}2{本|ほん}で{動|うご}く。
examples.english: This flashlight runs on two AA batteries.

notes:
{乾電池|かんでんち} specifically refers to disposable (non-rechargeable) dry cell batteries — the standard batteries used in remote controls, flashlights, toys, and other everyday devices.

FORMS:
{乾|かん} (dry) + {電池|でんち} (battery). "Dry" distinguishes it from older wet cell batteries.

COMMON SIZES (Japanese naming):
- {単三|たんさん}: AA (most common)
- {単四|たんよん}: AAA
- {単一|たんいち}: D
- {単二|たんに}: C

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {乾電池|かんでんち}を{入|い}れ{替|か}える: to replace batteries
- {乾電池|かんでんち}が{切|き}れる: batteries run out

RELATED WORDS:
- {充電池|じゅうでんち}/{充電式|じゅうでんしき}{電池|でんち}: rechargeable battery
- {電池切|でんちぎ}れ: dead battery
- ボタン{電池|でんち}: button cell battery
